source.title: The National Environmental Agency presented the results achieved in the areas of climate change adaptation and the development of early warning systems at COP31

capability_claims: The Agency says the COP31 presentation covered natural-hazard assessment and associated risks, hazard zoning, modernization of hydrometeorological observation and forecasting systems, development of early-warning mechanisms and digital transformation.
The Agency says the meteo.gov.ge mobile application provides meteorological and hydrological information and early warnings to the public, relevant state agencies and decision-makers.

The Agency reports expansion of the observation network, introduction of modern forecasting technologies and improved access to information about potential hazards under the GCF-supported, UNDP-implemented multi-hazard early-warning project.

The panel discussion addressed long-term system sustainability, integration of technology into operations, institutional capacity, regional cooperation and cross-border exchange of hydrometeorological data and forecasts.
not_established: The notice does not publish an observation-station inventory, count, hazard/region coverage, uptime, telemetry completeness or maintenance record.
The notice does not publish hazard-specific forecast-verification metrics, lead-time distributions, calibration or uncertainty measures.
The notice does not provide warning counts or separate denominators for issued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, understood, feasible and actioned warnings.
The notice does not report mobile-app reach, active-user counts, accessibility testing, language coverage, alert receipt or protective action.
The notice does not provide a counterfactual, avoided-loss estimate, mortality effect or independent audit of the reported capability improvements.
required_follow_up_metrics: Versioned station inventory by hazard and region, with active dates, uptime, data completeness, maintenance and metadata provenance.
Hazard-specific forecast verification by lead time, including probability of detection, false-alarm ratio, critical success index, calibration and uncertainty.
A warning-chain dataset with separate event/endpoint counts and denominators for issued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, understood, feasible and actioned stages.
Privacy-reviewed aggregate app and channel reach, language/accessibility coverage and offline-channel availability; never use person-level app telemetry in the public repository.
After-action review completeness, corrective-action closure and a predeclared comparison design before attributing changes in loss or mortality to the system.

fact: NEA published a 2026-11-16 notice describing its COP31 presentation and the capabilities it says have been developed.
The notice specifically names observation-network expansion, modern forecasting technologies, improved hazard-information access and the meteo.gov.ge mobile application.
inference: The next decision-relevant research question is not simply whether a warning system exists, but whether the reported capabilities deliver reliable and inclusive warning receipt and feasible protective action.
A mobile application and modernized observation network are enabling capabilities; neither alone establishes that exposed people receive, understand or can act on a warning.
hypothesis: If hazard-specific forecast quality, last-mile delivery, accessibility and feasible-action constraints are measured together, authorities may identify where additional investment produces the greatest protective benefit.
untested_idea: A privacy-preserving warning-chain dashboard could report separate aggregate stage metrics and data-quality flags without exposing individual recipients or exact household locations.
